{{Short description|Explanation for how quasars are powered}}
[[File:Active Black Hole Squashes Star Formation.jpg |thumb |An active galactic nucleus with relativistic jets.]]
The '''Blandford–Znajek process''' is a mechanism for the extraction of [[energy]] from a [[rotating black hole]],<ref>{{Citation |last1=Frolov |first1=Valeri P. |last2=Zelnikov |first2=Andrei |title=Introduction to Black Hole Physics |publisher=[[Oxford University Press]] |year=2011 |location=Oxford |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=r_l5AK9DdXsC&pg=PA34 |isbn=978-0-19-969229-3 |zbl=1234.83001}}, (Chapter 8.9: Black Holes in External Magnetic Field).</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Lea|first=Robert|date=2019-01-31|title=How black holes power relativistic jets|url=https://medium.com/predict/how-black-holes-power-relativistic-jets-aba4297c6b3d|access-date=2020-09-10|website=Medium|language=en}}</ref> introduced by [[Roger Blandford]] and [[Roman Znajek]] in 1977.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Blandford |first1=R. D. |last2=Znajek |first2=R. L. |date=1977-07-01 |title=Electromagnetic extraction of energy from Kerr black holes |journal=Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society |volume=179 |issue=3 |pages=433–456 |doi=10.1093/mnras/179.3.433 |doi-access=free |issn=0035-8711|arxiv=astro-ph/0506302 |bibcode=1977MNRAS.179..433B }}</ref> This mechanism is the most preferred description of how [[Astrophysical jet|astrophysical jets]] are formed around spinning [[Supermassive black hole|supermassive black holes]]. This is one of the mechanisms that power [[quasar]]s, or rapidly accreting supermassive black holes.<ref name="frank etal">{{Cite book|last1=Frank|first1=Juhan|last2=King|first2=Andrew|last3=Raine|first3=Derek J.|title=Accretion Power in Astrophysics|edition=Third|bibcode=2002apa..book.....F|isbn=0521620538 |location=Cambridge, UK |publisher=Cambridge University Press |date=February 2002}}</ref> Generally speaking, it was demonstrated that the power output of the accretion disk is significantly larger than the power output extracted directly from the hole, through its [[ergosphere]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Livio|first1=M.|last2=Ogilvie|first2=G. I.|last3=Pringle|first3=J. E.|date=1999-02-01|title=Extracting Energy from Black Holes: The Relative Importance of the Blandford-Znajek Mechanism|journal=The Astrophysical Journal|volume=512|issue=1|pages=100–104|doi=10.1086/306777|arxiv=astro-ph/9809093|bibcode=1999ApJ...512..100L|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=McKinney|first=Jonathan C.|date=2005-09-01|title=Total and Jet Blandford-Znajek Power in the Presence of an Accretion Disk|url=http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2005ApJ...630L...5M|journal=The Astrophysical Journal Letters|volume=630|issue=1|pages=L5–L8|doi=10.1086/468184|arxiv=astro-ph/0506367|bibcode=2005ApJ...630L...5M|s2cid=18743811}}</ref> Hence, the presence (or not) of a poloidal magnetic field around the black hole is not determinant in its overall power output. It was also suggested that the mechanism plays a crucial role as a central engine for a [[gamma-ray burst]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Lee|first1=H. K.|last2=Wijers|first2=R. A. M. J.|last3=Brown|first3=G. E.|date=2000|title=The Blandford-Znajek process as a central engine for a gamma-ray burst|url=http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2000PhR...325...83L|journal=Physics Reports|volume=325|issue=3|pages=83–114|doi=10.1016/S0370-1573(99)00084-8|arxiv=astro-ph/9906213|bibcode=2000PhR...325...83L|s2cid=7936182|issn=0370-1573}}</ref>

== Physics of the mechanism ==
[[File:Black hole jet diagram.jpg |thumb |Magnetic field lines around the jets of a quasar.]]
As in the [[Penrose process]], the [[ergosphere]] plays an important role in the Blandford–Znajek process. In order to extract energy and [[angular momentum]] from the black hole, the [[electromagnetic field]] around the hole must be modified by [[magnetospheric currents]]. In order to drive such currents, the electric field needs to not be screened, and consequently the vacuum field created within the ergosphere by distant sources must have an unscreened component. The most favored way to provide this is an e<sup>±</sup> pair cascade in a strong electric and radiation field.<ref>{{cite book|last=Camenzind|first=M.|title=Compact objects in Astrophysics|publisher=Springer|year=2007|isbn=978-3-540-25770-7|page=500, 505|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=6A9mngEACAAJ}}</ref> As the ergosphere causes the magnetosphere inside it to rotate, the outgoing flux of angular momentum results in extraction of energy from the black hole.

The Blandford–Znajek process requires an [[accretion disc]] with a strong [[Toroidal and poloidal|poloidal]] magnetic field around a spinning black hole. The [[magnetic field]] extracts spin energy, and the power can be estimated as the energy density at the speed of light cylinder times area:

: <math> P = B^2\left(\frac{r}{r_c}\right)^4 r_c c = \frac{B^2 r^4 \omega^2}{c},</math>

where ''B'' is the magnetic field strength, <math>r_c</math> is the [[Schwarzschild radius]], and ''ω'' is the [[angular velocity]].<ref name="frank etal" />

==See also==
* [[Penrose process]], another mechanism to extract energy from a black hole
* [[Hawking radiation]], another mechanism to extract mass, hence energy from a black hole
* [[Astrophysical jet|Astrophysical jets]], large structures seen around some quasars and created by the Blandford–Znajek process and/or the Penrose process
